It is a curious thing that no two people who have written about the marsh
agree on where it begins. Some say at the old mill, others at the line of
willows, and a few insist it has no beginning at all, only a slow change.

What is certain is that the water there is very still, and very dark, and
that the birds which live in it are not the birds of anywhere else. They
have longer legs and quieter voices, and they watch you as you pass.

The people of the nearby village do not go into the marsh after dark, and
they will not tell you why, only that their grandparents did not either,
and that the reasons were considered sufficient at the time and remain so.

There are no chapter headings in this account, no numbered sections, and
no capitalised banners announcing a new part. It is one continuous piece
of prose, which makes it a useful thing against which to test detection.
